title: People + AI: The New Dental Team Advantage
guest: Cory Pinegar, founder of REACH
summary: What if AI isn’t here to replace your dental team, but to help your best people do more?
body_html:
What if AI isn’t here to replace your dental team, but to help your best people do more?

In this episode of Raving Patients, Dr. Len Tau sits down with Cory Pinegar, founder of REACH, to explore how dental practices can combine great human talent with AI to work more efficiently without losing the personal connection patients value.

Staffing continues to be one of the biggest challenges facing dental practices, while AI is rapidly changing the way practices handle everything from patient communication to administrative work. Cory shares how virtual team members can take on important tasks such as insurance verification, recare, unscheduled treatment, and missed calls, giving in-office teams more time to focus on the patients in front of them.

The conversation also dives into AI and why Cory believes the future isn't about choosing between people and technology. Instead, the real opportunity is using AI to amplify good people, improve their performance, and help practices get more done.

Cory also shares how REACH uses AI for call coaching and insurance claims, what practices often get wrong when bringing on a virtual team member, and why culture, communication, and personality can be just as important as previous experience.

Looking ahead, Cory and Dr. Len discuss what the dental practice of the future could look like and why, as automation becomes more common, the human connection may become one of the most valuable parts of the patient experience.

What You'll Learn

  • How virtual team members can support a modern dental practice
  • Which tasks are a good fit for remote team members
  • Where virtual staffing can have the biggest impact on practice revenue
  • How AI and human team members can work together
  • Why AI can be an amplifier rather than a replacement for people
  • How AI is being used for call coaching and insurance claims
  • Why culture and communication can be more important than previous experience when hiring
  • What practices need to do to successfully onboard a virtual team member
  • Common mistakes practices make when adopting AI and remote staffing
  • What the dental practice of the future could look like
  • Why the human connection with patients may become even more valuable as technology advances

title: Get Found by Patients and AI: The New Rules of Dental Visibility
guest: Rita Zamora, founder of Connect90 and author of Get Found, Get Liked, Get Patients
summary: Your next patient may not find your dental practice through a traditional Google search.
body_html:
Your next patient may not find your dental practice through a traditional Google search. They may ask AI who the best dentist is, and what AI says about your practice will depend on the digital story you’re building right now.

In this episode of the Raving Patients Podcast, Dr. Len Tau welcomes back Rita Zamora, founder of Connect90 and author of Get Found, Get Liked, Get Patients, to discuss how AI is changing the way patients discover, evaluate, and choose dental practices. Rita explains why your website, reviews, social media, online listings, and other digital assets can no longer be treated separately. Together, they form an online ecosystem that helps both patients and AI determine whether your practice is credible, relevant, and worth recommending.

Rita and Dr. Len also break down the growing importance of review consistency, strategic social media content, online scheduling, and authentic photos and videos. They discuss why practices need to be intentional about what they want to be known for online, how AI is interpreting digital signals across multiple platforms, and why generic or heavily AI-generated content may actually work against your practice. If you want your practice to stay visible as AI-assisted search becomes part of the patient journey, this episode gives you practical steps to start preparing now.

title: The Associate Trap: Why Waiting Too Long to Own Can Cost Dentists a Fortune
guest: Brian Hanks, founder of Dental Buyer Advocates and author of How to Buy a Dental Practice
summary: Waiting until you “feel ready” to own a dental practice could be one of the most expensive decisions of your career.
body_html:
Waiting until you “feel ready” to own a dental practice could be one of the most expensive decisions of your career.

In this episode of the Raving Patients Podcast, Dr. Len Tau sits down with Brian Hanks, founder of Dental Buyer Advocates and author of How to Buy a Dental Practice, to talk about why younger dentists are waiting longer to become practice owners and what that delay could really cost them. Brian shares the numbers behind associate versus owner earnings, why student loan debt shouldn’t automatically keep dentists from ownership, and what the data actually says about the growth of DSOs.

Brian also breaks down how to evaluate a dental practice before buying, including the two simple questions every potential buyer should ask. He explains why a cheaper practice isn’t necessarily a better opportunity, how practice valuations work, and why paying above the national average can still be a smart investment. Plus, he shares what dentists who can’t seem to find the “right” practice may be overlooking.

title: Beyond Keywords and Bids: What Really Drives PPC Results
guest: Michael Lyjak, former Google trainer and founder of Efficiency Marketing
summary: Spending more money on Google Ads does not automatically mean more new patients. In fact, what happens after someone clicks your ad may matter just as much as the campaign itself.
body_html:
Spending more money on Google Ads does not automatically mean more new patients. In fact, what happens after someone clicks your ad may matter just as much as the campaign itself.

In this episode of the Raving Patients Podcast, Dr. Len Tau sits down with Michael Lyjak, former Google trainer and founder of Efficiency Marketing, to break down what really drives PPC performance for dental practices. Having managed more than $16 million in dental advertising since 2019 and worked with over 100 practices, Michael explains why successful paid advertising goes far beyond choosing the right keywords and setting a budget.

Michael shares how AI is changing Google Ads, why branded campaigns can actually help when structured correctly, and how reviews and a practice's overall digital footprint are becoming increasingly important to both paid and AI-driven search. He also explains quality score, budgeting based on market competition, and why Google leads typically cost more than Meta leads.

But getting the lead is only half the battle. Michael and Dr. Len discuss one of the biggest places dental practices lose marketing dollars: poor lead handling. Missed calls, slow response times, weak follow-up, and a lack of conversion tracking can turn even a well-performing ad campaign into wasted money. Michael explains why practices need a strong feedback loop between their marketing and front desk if they want to know what's actually generating appointments and revenue.

title: Your Front Desk Is Not Your Biller: The Hidden Revenue Leak Killing Independent Practices
guest: Ori Bekerman, founder of Practice Alpha
summary: Your practice can be producing plenty of dentistry and still be leaving a surprising amount of money on the table.
body_html:
Your practice can be producing plenty of dentistry and still be leaving a surprising amount of money on the table.

In this episode of the Raving Patients Podcast, Dr. Len Tau sits down with Ori Bekerman, founder of Practice Alpha, to uncover one of the most overlooked revenue leaks in independent dental practices: the billing process. After building, operating, and selling a multi-location dental group himself, Ori saw firsthand how easily revenue can get stuck in aging claims, inaccurate patient estimates, denied claims, and overloaded front desk workflows.

Ori breaks down the numbers every practice owner should be watching, including insurance and patient aging reports, collections, and claims over 90 days old. He explains why simply seeing claims go out and money come in doesn't mean your billing is healthy, and why accountability and consistent reporting are critical for identifying problems before they become expensive.
Dr. Len and Ori also discuss why asking your front desk to handle phones, scheduling, patient checkout, and billing at the same time can create costly mistakes. Ori shares how practices can evaluate whether billing should stay in-house or be outsourced, why EFT payments can improve cash flow, and how better revenue cycle management can help independent dentists protect profitability without constantly chasing more new patients.

  • How to tell if your dental practice has a billing or collections problem
  • The key insurance and patient aging numbers every practice owner should monitor

title: Your Vendors Have the Keys: The Cyber Risk Dental Practices Ignore
guest: Anthony Jurjevic, CISSP, founder and CEO of Techspedient
summary: The biggest cybersecurity threat to your dental practice may not be a hacker trying to break through your firewall. It could be a vendor you already trust.
body_html:
The biggest cybersecurity threat to your dental practice may not be a hacker trying to break through
your firewall. It could be a vendor you already trust.

In this episode of the Raving Patients Podcast, Dr. Len Tau sits down with Anthony Jurjevic, CISSP, founder and CEO of Techspedient, to uncover the cybersecurity risks many dental practices do not realize are already inside their networks. With more than 25 years in healthcare IT and cybersecurity, including over 15 years focused on dental technology, Anthony explains why vendor access, outdated credentials, shared passwords, and poorly managed remote access tools can leave practices vulnerable.

Anthony explains how practice management companies, imaging vendors, billing services, patient communication platforms, phone systems, and other vendors may have ongoing access to a practice's network. The problem is not necessarily that these vendors are unsafe. It is that many practices do not know who still has access, how that access is being monitored, or what happens if a vendor's credentials are compromised.

The conversation also tackles one of the biggest misconceptions in dental cybersecurity: being in the cloud does not automatically mean your practice is backed up or secure. Anthony shares how attackers can compromise a workstation, use saved credentials to access cloud-based patient information, and quietly steal data without encrypting an entire network. He explains why modern ransomware attacks increasingly focus on data theft and extortion, making traditional backups only one piece of a much larger security strategy.
Dr. Len and Anthony also discuss HIPAA compliance, what happens after a ransomware attack, the importance of cyber insurance and forensic investigations, and the practical steps dentists can take right now to identify vulnerabilities. From auditing vendor access and removing former employees to testing backups, enabling multi-factor authentication, and conducting third-party cybersecurity assessments, this episode gives practice owners a practical look at protecting both their patients and their businesses.

What You'll Learn

  • Why trusted vendors can become one of your biggest cybersecurity vulnerabilities
  • How unattended remote access can expose your dental practice
  • Why being "in the cloud" does not automatically make your data safe
  • How modern ransomware has shifted from encrypting data to stealing it
  • Why backups cannot protect you once patient data has already been stolen
  • What "HIPAA compliant" software really means for a dental practice
  • What to do immediately after discovering a possible ransomware attack
  • Why individual user accounts are safer than shared passwords
  • How to audit vendor access, administrative permissions, and former employee accounts
  • Why multi-factor authentication should be enabled wherever possible
  • How penetration testing can reveal weaknesses before an attacker finds them

title: The Hidden Revenue Sitting in Your Recall List
guest: Aman Garg, founder of 10X Dental
summary: What if one of the biggest growth opportunities in your dental practice isn't finding more new patients, but bringing back the patients you already have?
body_html:
What if one of the biggest growth opportunities in your dental practice isn't finding more new patients, but bringing back the patients you already have?

In this episode of the Raving Patients Podcast, Dr. Len Tau sits down with Aman Garg, founder of 10X Dental, to talk about the hidden revenue sitting inside overdue and unscheduled hygiene lists. While many practices invest heavily in new patient acquisition, hundreds of existing patients may quietly fall out of their recall system simply because they are busy, don't respond to automated texts, or never get consistent follow-up.

Aman explains how AI can help practices scale outbound recall without replacing the relationships patients have with the front desk, hygienists, and doctors. He shares data from 10X Dental's recall efforts, including a 16% average scheduling rate, an 85% attendance rate among scheduled patients, and an average of $450 in reactivation production per returning patient.
Dr. Len and Aman also discuss why traditional recall systems often fall short, how practices can create a consistent recall strategy, the importance of confirmation sequences, and where AI fits into the patient experience. They also explore the limits of automation and why using AI effectively should feel like helping the patient rather than simply filling holes in the schedule.

title: Beyond the PMS: What Dentists Need to Know About Data, Benchmarks, and Profit
guest: Vin Cardillo, founder of Pronto Dental
summary: Your practice management software holds plenty of data, but is it giving you the insights you actually need to grow?
body_html:
Your practice management software holds plenty of data, but is it giving you the insights you actually need to grow? In this episode, Dr. Len Tau sits down with Vin Cardillo, founder of Pronto Dental, to discuss why tracking the right metrics matters more than simply collecting data. From profitability and benchmarking to missed phone calls and perio performance, Vin shares how dentists can make smarter decisions, improve accountability, and build more profitable practices by understanding the numbers behind their business.

Most dental practices already have access to a wealth of information, but many struggle to turn that information into meaningful action. Dr. Len Tau welcomes Vin Cardillo, founder of Pronto Dental, to explain why relying solely on practice management software can leave major blind spots in your business.

Vin shares how aggregating data from multiple systems including practice management, accounting, HR, reputation management, and phone systems creates a clearer picture of practice performance. He explains how benchmarking helps identify opportunities for improvement and why focusing on a handful of high-impact metrics can dramatically increase profitability.

The conversation also explores common areas where practices lose revenue, including missed phone calls, low periodontal treatment rates, accounts receivable, and underutilized production capacity. Vin discusses the importance of accountability, consistent SOPs, reviewing monthly financials, and using data to build confidence as a business owner. Whether you're a solo practitioner or growing multiple locations, this episode offers practical insights to help you run a healthier, more profitable dental practice.

title: Stop Blaming the Leads: How Dental Practices Can Convert More Big Cases
guest: Tim Hines, President of Briteline Dental
summary: What if the problem isn’t your marketing, but what happens after the lead comes in?
body_html:
What if the problem isn’t your marketing, but what happens after the lead comes in? Too many dental practices spend thousands on ads only to watch potential patients disappear because of slow follow-up, poor communication, and broken systems. What if your biggest growth opportunity isn’t your marketing… but how your team communicates?

In this episode, Dr. Len Tau sits down with returning guest Danny Bobrow to break down the human side of practice growth. From the first phone call to treatment acceptance, Danny explains why trust, empathy, and communication skills are the real drivers behind case acceptance and long-term patient loyalty.

They dive into why most practices mishandle leads, how emotional decision-making impacts patient behavior, and the simple shifts your team can make to create stronger connections that lead to more yeses.

If you want better conversions, stronger relationships, and a more consistent patient experience, this episode is a must-listen.
